question.text: Chambal Managed Futures Fund (Cat III AIF, CTA / managed-futures style) wishes to select a global peer benchmark for its PPM. Which of the following is the MOST widely-used hedge-fund index family produced by Hedge Fund Research, Inc. and structured by strategy (e.g., Macro, Equity Hedge, Event-Driven, Relative Value)?

explanation.text: The Logic: Hedge Fund Research, Inc. (HFRI) is widely recognised as a leading publisher of hedge-fund peer indices, with strategy-tiered sub-indices such as HFRI Macro, HFRI Equity Hedge, HFRI Event-Driven, HFRI Relative Value, and the HFRI Fund Weighted Composite. These are the industry-standard global peer benchmarks for hedge-fund / CTA strategies. The Trap: Options B (MSCI World), C (S&P Global BMI) and D (FTSE Russell Government Bond) are legitimate broad market indices for equity or bonds, but none is a hedge-fund peer index. Note: HFRI, Hedge Fund Research, and the specific HFRI strategy sub-index families are not explicitly named in the cited XIX-E (Category III AIF Managers) workbook pages, which support CTA/managed-futures, global equity/bond indices, and Indian AIF benchmarking-agency concepts generally. The framing above reflects general industry knowledge of global hedge-fund index providers.
